name: cURL Generator
description: Assemble a cURL command from method, headers, authentication and body; passwords and tokens appear as placeholders only.

hints.url: The URL is required; GET does not produce an extra -X GET.
hints.headers: A header marked "Use a placeholder" has its value replaced by <header name>, so the plain value never reaches the command.
hints.auth: A Basic password and a Bearer token are placeholders as well; the plain value never ends up in the result.
hints.insecure: Skipping certificate verification weakens security; use it only to debug self-signed certificates.
hints.placeholders: Replace the placeholders in the command with your real values locally.
hints.output: Arguments are quoted for the target shell, so the command can be pasted into a terminal as is.

faq.q: Why is my password missing from the command?
faq.a: Passwords, tokens and headers marked sensitive are always rendered as placeholders such as <PASSWORD> and <TOKEN>, so plain credentials are never pasted into a chat window or committed to a script.

faq.q: Does the body format change the command?
faq.a: Yes. Form and JSON bodies are passed with --data-raw, raw bodies with --data-binary.

faq.q: Why does the GET request have no -X flag?
faq.a: GET is the default method and is left out; every other method gets an -X flag.
